name: Paiute
description: Paiute is a Hawaiian draw-and-discard game similar to Knock Poker. Players draw and discard to form five- or six-card poker combinations. A turn-up card sets the wild rank. Unique: a player can call with a six-card hand (Three Pairs, called Paiute) on their first draw only.

overview.description: Paiute is a Hawaiian draw-and-discard game similar to Knock Poker. Players draw and discard to form five- or six-card poker combinations. A turn-up card sets the wild rank. Unique: a player can call with a six-card hand (Three Pairs, called Paiute) on their first draw only.

history.origins: Hawaiian game; documented from contributions by Derek Bal, Malia Pugh, and Pomai T.
timeline: 2000s: Documented on card-game websites and United Poker Forum.
Present: Played in Hawaii and by enthusiasts elsewhere.
history.evolution: Variants include Joker-as-wild, opposite-colour wilds only, Royal Flush over Five of a Kind, and six-player Paiute-any-time.

setup.players: Two to five players use a standard international 52-card pack; ace ranks high. Five cards are dealt to each player; the next card is turned face up to set the wild rank for that deal.
setup.dealing: Five cards to each player. Next card turned face up becomes the wild card (e.g. 3 â†’ all 3s wild). Remainder stacked face down with wild card partly visible = stock.
setup.equipment: Standard deck, chips or money for stakes.

rules.objective: Form the highest five- or six-card combination and call to win the pot.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Turn**: Draw one (stock or discard top), discard one. Hand stays at 5 cards until a call. 2. **Call**: With a winning combination after drawing, place it face up. Five-card: discard your 6th card. Six-card: no discard; next player draws from stock or your discard. 3. **Round completion**: If caller is not the dealer, play continues so each player up to and including dealer gets one turn. 4. **Later calls**: Others may call if they equal or beat the best shown. 5. **Winner**: Highest combination wins the pot. Equal hands split the pot (or first-caller wins in some variants).
keyRules: Turn-up card sets the wild rank for that deal.
Winning combinations: 5 or 6 cards. No value for mixed-suit straights or non-sequence flushes.
Paiute (Three Pairs) can only be called on a player's first draw (first round).
If stock runs out, shuffle discard (except top) to form new stock.
Pick from discard = must discard a different card; pick from stock = may discard the drawn card.

strategy.basic: Track the wild rank and build toward Five of a Kind or Four/Two. Avoid discarding cards that help opponents.
strategy.intermediate: Consider calling early with a strong hand vs waiting to improve; balance pot odds with risk of others improving.
strategy.advanced: Model opponent draws; time calls to maximize value when dealer has weak holdings.
tips: Paiute (Three Pairs) is a strong first-draw call; don't pass it if you have it.
With wilds, Four/Two and Five of a Kind are realistic; prioritize those.
Straights and flushes (mixed suit) have no valueâ€”discard them.

scoring.description: Stakes game. Each player antes; winner takes the pot. Some variants use scaled payments by hand rank.
scoring.winCondition: Player with the highest called combination wins the pot.

synthesis.shortDescription: Hawaiian draw-and-discard. Turn-up sets wilds. Call with 5- or 6-card combinations; Paiute (Three Pairs) only on first draw.
